questions.question: Xu’s notification formats in scope are:
options: Only carrier pigeons and fax machines.
Mobile push, SMS, and email.
Only in-process log lines with no user delivery.
Only browser localStorage writes on the same device.
questions.explanation: mobile push notification, SMS message, and Email

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide by Alex Xu
reference.excerpt: A notification is more than just mobile push notification. Three types of notification formats are: mobile push notification, SMS message, and Email.

questions.question: iOS push delivery commonly goes through:
options: A random public MQTT broker with no auth.
Apple Push Notification Service (APNS) using device token + payload.
Direct SMS gateways that ignore device tokens.
FTP uploads to each phone overnight.

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide by Alex Xu
reference.excerpt: Here is an example: • APNS: This is a remote service provided by Apple to propagate push notifications to iOS devices. • iOS Device: It is the end client, which receives push notifications.

questions.question: Android push in Xu’s overview commonly uses:
options: APNS exclusively for all Android devices.
Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) as a common path.
APNS exclusively for all Android devices as well.
Direct SQL inserts into the phone’s SQLite over the open internet.
questions.explanation: Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) is commonly used

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide by Alex Xu
reference.excerpt: Instead of using APNs, Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) is commonly used to send push notifications to android devices.

questions.question: Contact info gathering stores device tokens separately because:
options: A user can have multiple devices that should all receive pushes.
Device tokens must never be associated with a user id.
Email and SMS cannot be stored in any database table.
APNS forbids persisting tokens longer than one second.
questions.explanation: A user can have multiple devices

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide by Alex Xu
reference.excerpt: Contact info gathering flow To send notifications, we need to gather mobile device tokens, phone numbers, or email addresses.

questions.question: True or false: Users who opt out should stop receiving notifications.
questions.explanation: users who choose to opt-out will no longer receive notifications

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide by Alex Xu
reference.excerpt: Notification system: The notification system is the centerpiece of sending/receiving notifications.

questions.question: Calling the system “soft real-time” means:
options: Messages may be delayed forever with no delivery goal.
Deliver ASAP, but slight delay under high load is acceptable.
Every notification must arrive within one microsecond worldwide.
Notifications only send when the on-call engineer presses a button.
questions.explanation: soft real-time… slight delay is acceptable

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide by Alex Xu
reference.excerpt: However, if the system is under a high workload, a slight delay is acceptable.

books.book: Fundamentals of Software Architecture, 2nd Edition by Mark Richards and Neal Ford
books.excerpt: If those calls fail, it impacts the reliability of the calling system.
